text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz Make sure you know what you are getting yourself into before purchasing this item. I think it is a great item for the right person/people. If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz

Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab These days with many kids doing home schooling due to lockdowns, this would be a great home schoolilng science project or lesson.

The age recommendation is for children six and up, however since most of these experiments require the use of a pot of boiling water, I think the manufacturer should increase the age requirement. Parental supervision is of course a great idea. The booklet is easy to understand, however it might be more difficult for younger children to read and understand the instructions.

I only tried the first experiment in the kit and it worked as expected, and it was the easiest, fastest experiment to get results. The instructions were easy to follow. (I also lacked any distilled water which many of the experiment recipes call for). It was fun for me as an adult to try.

I am not sure if this is an option or not, but it would be nice if refills on the "magic water, colors, (maybe even some not available in this kit) and paper cones) were made available so kids (or adults) can continue to keep playing and making different crystals. (Alum powder and food coloring are both readily available at any grocer.)

The box is attractively marked and would make a great gift for any adult or child who likes science or educational toys. This kit is compatible with other chemistry sets available from the same company.

All in all, it's a fun, educational kit that anyone can enjoy. The only true down side is that it may try the patience of kids who like instant results. Some of these experiments take two or three days to have decent crystals develop. I liked the kit and found it fascinating. I can't wait to try the other experiments in the kit.

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.
text_fidelity_b: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set I absolutely love this swingset. We ordered it from Costco, because the price was a bit lower. We already had the matching jungle gym, so we didn't really want to get the larger monkey bar swingset. I found this one and thought it was perfect. I was right. Assembly was a bear. Based solely on the weight of the pieces, you need a few people to put this together. It takes some maneuvering to get the pieces together and in place, but once they are together, they are solid. The swings and ring were a bit high for my 4 year old, so we picked up four 6 inch sections of chain from the local hardware store and some quick links. Problem solved. We left one of the swings higher for the older kids. My son and I swing on it together, and it only moves a bit. We will likely anchor it in the future, but for small children, it stays in place well enough. The coating on the swings is much better than the normal covered chains which crack and come apart. This is thick rubbery substance that fully wraps around the chains. We didn't use the feet on the bottom as it allows the set to settle into the ground a bit as we use it. The set looks professional, not tacky, and unlike wood sets, I won't be out there trying to clean it and check for splinters constantly. I can see this being used for generations. Great item. Seems like commercial quality.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set

text_fidelity_a: Warashibe Wooden Secret Puzzle Box, 5 Sun 21 Steps, Japan Made, with Original Gift Box I have some from the 1940s that my father brought home from World War II.  One is more traditional - it is made of wood and looks like a stack of faux books with a larger book on its side both on the bottom and top.  The "page" piece of the bottom book slides open to an area that holds the key, the bottom book slides back, the center book's spine slides down to reveal the keyhole.  Insert the key, turn it and the book on top opens to a velvet lined interior.  The top book has several veneers to create a border and little birds flying across the top.  My other puzzle box has a large veneered diamond on top of the heavily veneered box.  Slide the diamond back and the box can be opened.  Center the diamond on the closed box and it "locks" it.  This box is more complicated that either of my other puzzle boxes mentioned here, but one thing they all share in common is the veneer work.  This box features very geometric veneering and it is quite pretty.  The complexity of the puzzle to open the box is a lot more fun and interesting for this box - it's really neat!  Yes, they are expensive, but for a reason - the veneer work and all the moving parts of this box requires a seriously high amount of quality control.  Worth it, for sure!

Digital Coin Bank Savings Jar - Automatic Coin Counter Totals All U.S. Coins Including Dollars and Half Dollars - Original Style, Transparent Pink Jar UPDATE 6-20-2016:

Filltech read my review and reached out to me to make things right. I really appreciated that! They sent a replacement bank free of charge as the one I received was defective and wouldn't count coins right. The replacement is 100% working and is not as hard to insert the coins. It counts them as fast as you can put them in and it gets the pennies and dimes right every time. I recommend this bank and seller because if it's defective, they will make it right!

I had somewhat high hopes for this coin bank, but it's not 100% accurate. It's main problem is distinguishing between dimes and pennies. As far as I can tell it has a lever that is supposed to detect the size of the coin and add that denomination to the total. It doesn't always work. Dimes and pennies get miscounted no matter how slow or fast you put them in. I put in $2 worth pennies and the count was $2.64 because of it counting some of the pennies as dimes. I corrected the count, then added some dimes, which at least four of them were counted as pennies. I think it's overpriced for this reason. If it kept a better count and the jar was glass and came with batteries....then it would be worth $18. As it stands now it's maybe a $5 bank. It might be alright for some people and I like the design and size of it, but probably will pass on buying it again.

We took this to a family baby blessing and had the cousins not squabbled over it, the board would have kept my son very quiet! (And I mean things quickly deteriorated into a 5-cousin brawl of boys and girls ages 2-7 until the board was put away because everyone wanted it!)

Children LOOOOVE making rubber band designs and this 11x11 inch board allows for some cool ones. You can buy colored rubber bands on Amazon but I recommend grabbing a bag of neon bright bands for under five at an office supply store. The very few (like 12 total?) it came with were a rubber-eraser reddish-pink, dusty white and vintage spearmint green. They are fairly gross looking colors and except for the white, the rest reside permanently in the bottom of the rubber band bag.

When it arrived our board was yellow, which I liked MUCH better than the red shown but be aware you'll get a random color. The one we just ordered in October 2013 for a cousin christmas gift (since it was such a hit!) was also yellow. Every time my son pulls it out in church, children in the pews in front of us and behind us begin quietly peeking over his work to see what he's making with that contraption and everyone wants a turn! If you need a fun toy for kids of all ages that won't break the bank, doesn't require batteries or make any noise and builds brain cells while you play, this is it!
text_fidelity_b: Learning Resources Single-Sided Geoboard 11 x 11 Pin

Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue We enjoyed using this kit. I did it mostly with my 7 and 10 year old children. My 7 year old was the most interested. My 5 year old had interest, but he wasn't as gentle with it as he needed to be.

I especially like that the projects are centered around a story. You read a little, then build, read, build..... It makes the whole thing more fun and puts things into perspective. Everything you need is provided in the box, except for 2 AA batteries(so have those on hand before starting). The projects can get a little complicated, particularly when the gears come into the story, but it's not too bad. Some children might need help(or it can simply be a challenge to see if they can figure it out on their own).

The quality is mostly nice. The treehouse is made out of sheets of wood, and it seems durable to me. It won't last through rough play, but for the project, it holds up well. When building the treehouse, you can glue the pieces into place. We chose to take it apart, so we could do the projects again later with my youngest child. (Untying the knots was a bit of a pain, but otherwise, it's pretty simple to take apart.) There are a few pieces that are paper, though, and these are much less durable.

If you're looking for a fun project for a rainy day of learning, this is a nice kit to try.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue

The battery for the copter charged quickly. The batteries for the controls come with, but you'll need a tiny screwdriver to get them in.

Flying inside is easier than outside, though completely not recommended. The copter is so light, it is susceptible to the gentlest wind. The controls are very hair-sensitive, making it difficult to steer with any accuracy. As such, fly in a large field. Otherwise, expect it stuck in a tree, land on a roof, or be busted up on the street.

Extra blades are included. After a few crashes, I can see they'll be necessary. I don't expect it to be durable with any extended use.

I'm giving it three stars because it does work as advertised. Overall, however, I'm unimpressed.

anthonytrendl.com

We now have a well established family tradition of puzzling with increasingly challenging puzzles. For the last few years, only Ravensburgers will do. These puzzles are well made, with thick, solid cardboard with a bright, spill resistant color.

The difficult part about this puzzle are the vast blue and cloudy blue areas at the top, and the large amounts of snow covered tree limbs. I would judge this puzzle as on the "difficult" end for puzzles with 2,000 pieces (to be precise, it has 2,040 pieces!). It took our family a full week to work through all the branches, blues, snow, etc.

A nice thing about this puzzle is that even though its 2,000 pieces, the pieces are all a "large" nice size, which makes it more fun, and easier to tell one from another, and spot tiny differences in color and shape.

The insert in the box comes in a wide variety of languages, the pieces come inside the sturdy box wrapped in a bag. Its quality throughout.

Have fun!

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 120" X 72" X 22", for Ages 6+ We purchased this pool together with the following products:

- Intex The Wet Set Rectangular Pool Cover
- Intex 120V AC Quickfill Pump
- 10'X12' HD Tarp
- Associated pool toys

Set up was made quick and easy by matching the large opening on the pump with each of the three large intake openings on the pool to get all three levels quickly filled with air, starting at the bottom as per the directions. After laying out the tarp the pool unfolded quickly and we centered it over the tarp prior to inflating. We followed the suggestions of other reviewers to use the smaller tip on the pump with the smaller valve openings on the pool to finalize the air fill so as not to over inflate. The entire setup process couldn't have taken more than 15-20 minutes. Very easy.

It took another 20-25 minutes to fill the pool with a garden hose to the fill line clearly marked inside the pool. With a 90 degree day outside in the sun we could have done without adding any hot water but we did put in a couple pots anyway. We also added a cup of household bleach to the pool as one reviewer suggested. Undoubtedly there are better ways of keeping the water clean and we'll research those as we go along. We simply wanted to get up and running quickly the first time as our 5 year old couldn't wait.

Wouldn't have set this pool up any other way. The electric air pump made inflation of the three levels very quick and easy. I would recommend a tarp (they're quite inexpensive at Lowes or Home Depot), and while you could use a bed sheet as a pool cover we're quite satisfied with the Intex product.

Just a reminder - there's a single drain valve in the bottom corner of the pool. Remember to close that prior to filling. I forgot to do it and as I began filling the pool I thought it had arrived with a leak. Doh!

Keep in mind that this is a day 1 review. Cleaning, etc., may dampen our enthusiasm but if this pool lasts through the summer it will have been well worth the investment.

The only complaint we have after our first really fun day with this pool is that Amazon lowered the price by $5 the day after ours arrived. That's the second time this has happened to us with an Amazon purchase. While it's only $5 it is irksome.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 120" X 72" X 22", for Ages 6+

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn I've bought some of the Alex Toys for the children in our family, but this is the first Alex Junior Toy we've owned. Alex Toys are known for their sturdiness, well made enough to pass on to future generations, wonderful educational and imagination values and gorgeous vivid colors. This beautiful barn is no exception with it's sturdiness, educational value and vivid bright colors.

This barn is very sturdy, weighing over 10 pounds and made of both very smooth wood and wood products. You can easily see this lasting for future generations of babies to learn with. There are 6 sides of the barn for learning and play. The 2 sides of the roof are beautifully colored with numbers and corresponding food items- such as the number 8, shows eight ears of corn. One side of the barn has 3 barn doors that when opened, baby can see the animals living inside. The other side of the barn, has a windmill, cloud and sun that, being gears, all turn each other when moved.

The large back of the barn has a moveable tractor, cow and rooster. Baby can move these inside the tracks, so nothing comes loose. The front of the barn includes the most wonderful spinning wood blocks of the alphabet with accompanying pictures. There is a darling owl for the letter O, a cute donkey for the letter D and all the pictures that accompany the letters of the alphabet are not only adorable, but beautifully colored. We have twins in our family and this barn being 6 sided allows them to play on different sides at the same time.

I remember wood alphabet blocks being passed down from one generation to another in our family, but this gorgeous barn will replace that tradition. This barn makes it easy and fun for baby to learn both the alphabet and their numbers at the same time. Our babies love the vivid colors and they love learning that 2 means counting 2 items and that the sound of the letter J sounds like Jam. This is a beautiful barn that your baby will love learning their ABC's and 123's with. It's 5 Star Learning Fun that will last many generations to come.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn

Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends MINIS playset with 3 action-Packed stunt tracks! Great toy. Easy to assemble and good quality. Instructions are easy to follow. Took me about 15 mins. Does not come with batteries.

Pros:
1) easy assembly
2) holds out son’s attention span for about 30 mins
3) light weight and easy handling by toddler
4) easy storage- doesn’t take up a lot of room
5) 3 different race tracks with inter changeable track section
6) easy system to understand for a 2.5 year old

Cons (1 star deduction):
1) design flaws: if child feeds too many minis into the track it tends to creat a jam at the starting point and stop the track (easy fix: remove the minis)
2) design flaw: it also knocks off the minis if jammed
3) the interchangeably track part tends to create a jam if not lined up exactly and one has to be quick. A child might not have enough agility to be quick changing the track creating a jam if too many minis on the track.

No toy is perfect. With that said our son loves it and even we enjoy playing with it. That is all that counts and seeing the joy on his face is all this needs. It so worth purchasing this.

We use the mini as rewards system for our son’s potty training. He enjoys playing with them so much that we decided to get him the track before Christmas 🎄

Tegu Robo Magnetic Wooden Block Set, Electric Aqua, 8 PIECE We received our first Tegu product in a Citrus Lane Subscription box. It was just 4 triangle shaped pieces. They were great, and I wanted to try more without getting a huge set in case they lost their luster with my son, which tends to happen with kids. We ordered this set to go along with the 4 pieces we already had.

The wood is lightweight and smooth. It is almost soft to the touch. The dyes used are non toxic. The magnets are safe since they are encased.

This set is great. My son likes robots, so the Robo look on the side of these blocks added to the fun. He can rearrange them into various new robots. We stick these in a busy bag for church, and they keep him occupied most Sundays.

We will most likely end up with more Tegu. The cost seems reasonable for a humanely produced toy made from quality materials.

The only problem we have is that sometimes the poles of the magnets don't line up, so they do not attract. We are used to Magformers and don't have that problem with those. I would still recommend these and consider them a go to gift for preschoolers.

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Reading - Learn to Read Preschool Workbook with Interactive Pen, Kids Travel Activity, Ages 3+ We are really loving these Hot Dots learning activity books. My preschooler loves letters, so this reading book is great for getting some practice in. I love that it covers what you’d expect with matching letters, but also includes other things like rhyming, what happens next themes, letters that start and end in certain sounds, as well as other concepts.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Reading - Learn to Read Preschool Workbook with Interactive Pen, Kids Travel Activity, Ages 3+

Fisher-Price Imaginext Mega T-Rex My little boy is almost 3, and he loves this toy! My husband and I have even had fun with it, but probably just because our son gets so excited when the little missiles shoot up in the air. That would probably be the only warning I would have with it. For a toy, the missiles can go a good little distance, and could possible poke someone in the eye. The chances are most likely low, but it could happen.

The only thing that I somewhat didn't like is there's no directions. We just had to figure out on our own and by looking at picture on the box where the extras attached. It didn't take forever or anything, but it was annoying trying to guess at where the pieces went. That is a very minor issue, though!

The dinosaur doesn't really do a whole lot, but I think it's great for creative play. You have to hold the button down for it to roar, and as soon as you let go, it stops. As a parent, I actually really like that feature. I hate when you mash a button and have to listen to noise for several minutes. As I mentioned earlier, there are two missiles that you can launch into the air. There's also a little man that rides on the dinosaur's back. He sits in a compartment. The little flap that keeps him in this compartment comes off really easily and that annoyed my son, but it goes back on easily, too.

We like this toy so much for my son that we're planning on adding to our collection from the same line of toys this Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Imaginext Mega T-Rex

QUOKKA Giant Outdoor Stacking Game for Family This package came with three wooden puzzles: Arctic animals, outer space, and construction trucks. Each puzzle has 26-28 pieces. The construction trucks puzzle is the simplest because it has the 26 pieces and it's obvious which pieces go to which truck. The animals puzzle is only a little more difficult. The outer space puzzle is more difficult unless you know the order of the planets. It would have been nice to have a picture of what you're putting together on that one. Each corner piece can be identified by words or such so that you know which corner to put it in. That helps the puzzle get started. There is a notch in the top, right corner to help you get started with pulling the pieces out (or, of course, you can turn it upside down). The backboard on the Arctic animals came slightly warped, but the others were fine. They do make a point of storing the puzzles between 40 and 60% humidity.

It looks like the pieces have been laser cut out of one piece of wood. The pieces are about 3 mm thick, and they feel sturdier than a cardboard puzzle. The picture has been lightly painted on the wood. Generally, the pieces are easy to pull apart and put together. The first time I worked the puzzle, some pieces were a little stuck together, but they seemed fine the second time. I got these for my four-years-old niece. These seem to be about the right level for her as the different pieces are different enough in shape and it's fairly clear what part of the picture is on them. The pieces were fitted together tightly enough, though, that she sometimes needed an adult to help properly align them to get them to fit. When you take the pieces out, the backboard is blank (no suggested shapes to help very young puzzle workers).
text_fidelity_b: QUOKKA Giant Outdoor Stacking Game for Family

text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining My children have enjoyed various kinds of dig kits in the past, so they were excited for this one, too. My 5 year old got this one, and he liked it pretty well.

On my side, though, this particular kit wasn't one of my favorites. The kit comes with a hammer, but that thing was absolutely useless! My child was frustrated with it, so I gave it a try. Useless! The description tells you that you'll get a pair of goggles, but you don't. There's no goggles in this kit, but the instructions recommend that your child wear a pair. Also, I dislike that all of the rocks were clumped in one little spot in ours, and that happen to be right where my child started digging. He got them all dug out very quickly, but still had a great deal of clay to dig through. Discovering "treasures" slowly(at least more slowly than this one) is the whole fun of these things.

Like all dig kits, this one is messy. We've found shallow pie pans to be the best holders. The sides aren't too tall, so it won't hurt your child's arms. It also keeps the mess inside the pan. For the kits that are harder to dig, it makes it super easy to move the dig until your child wants to work on it again. This particular dig is on the softer side, though not the softest we've ever done. Really, it's just right in that area, for our tastes. It's not so hard that it's frustrating, but not so soft that the dig ends in a few minutes(or it wouldn't have if ours had the gems spaced out better).

Overall, if your child enjoys rocks(or gems), this is a decent choice. There are better options, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining

I bought the $5.99 blue version and I love it. I had my doubts at first but bought it for my grandson, so the small size was a requirement.
